title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in healthcare settings, yet their tendency to hallucinate poses risks when clinical decisions are involved. This study examine whether LLMs recommend recently banned or withdrawn pharmaceuticals when answering clinical questions and tests an agent-based method for reducing such errors. We developed a five-agent "Trust but Verify" system using a single LLM backbone. To measure regulatory knowledge obsolescence, we created an adversarial dataset of 103 clinical MCQs where historically correct answers now refer to banned substances. This scale ensures statistical significance across various therapeutic classes. We evaluated three open-access model families (GPT-OSS, Llama-3, Falcon-3) under vanilla and agentic conditions. Performance was measured via pointwise score, label accuracy, Hallucination Error Rate (HER), and Component Fidelity (CF) score. We also observed clinical safety regression in proprietary models. In default configurations, all models showed high hallucination rates, consistently selecting banned drugs that matched training data patterns. Our proposed agentic architecture reduced HER by approximately 53% across models. Pointwise scores shifted from -0.25 (unsafe recommendation) toward 0.0 (appropriate refusal). The safety audit intercepted dangerous outputs even when models' parametric knowledge favored the banned substance. The proposed multi-agent framework offers a model-agnostic method for enforcing regulatory compliance that prioritizes patient safety over fluent text generation. Our work demonstrates a practical approach for deploying autonomous AI systems in safety-critical healthcare settings. It shows how real-time regulatory data can be integrated into LLM pipelines to support clinical decision-making.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-agent 'Trust but Verify' system using a single LLM backbone to reduce medical hallucinations, achieving a ~53% reduction in hallucination error rate on an adversarial dataset of banned drug questions.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于单一LLM后端的五智能体“信任但验证”系统，用于减少医疗幻觉，在关于禁用药物的对抗性数据集上实现了约53%的幻觉错误率降低。
summary_zh: 大型语言模型（LLMs）正越来越多地被部署在医疗场景中，但当涉及临床决策时，其产生幻觉的倾向会带来风险。本研究考察了LLMs在回答临床问题时是否会推荐近期被禁用或撤市的药物，并测试了一种基于代理的方法以减少此类错误。我们开发了一个基于单一LLM骨干的“信任但验证”五代理系统。为衡量监管知识的过时程度，我们构建了一个包含103道临床多项选择题的对抗性数据集，其中历史正确答案现指代违禁物质。该规模确保了跨多种治疗类别的统计显著性。我们在原始设置和代理条件下评估了三个开源模型系列（GPT-OSS、Llama-3、Falcon-3）。性能通过逐点得分、标签准确率、幻觉错误率（HER）和组件保真度（CF）得分进行衡量。我们还观察了专有模型在临床安全性上的退化。在默认配置下，所有模型均表现出高幻觉率，持续选择与训练数据模式匹配的违禁药物。我们提出的代理架构将各模型的HER降低了约53%。逐点得分从-0.25（不安全推荐）移至接近0.0（适当拒绝）。即使模型的参数知识倾向于违禁物质，安全审计也能拦截危险输出。所提出的多代理框架提供了一种模型无关的方法来强制执行监管合规性，将患者安全置于流畅文本生成之上。我们的工作展示了在安全关键的医疗场景中部署自主AI系统的实用方法，并说明了如何将实时监管数据集成到LLM流程中以支持临床决策。

title: MedLatentDx: Latent Multi-Agent Communication for Cross-Hospital Rare-Disease Diagnosis
summary: Rare diseases affect over $300$ million patients across more than $7{,}000$ conditions, yet no single hospital encounters enough cases of any one condition for reliable diagnosis. Cross-hospital collaboration could help by allowing a diagnosing institution to use distributed, case-specific diagnostic evidence, but privacy regulations restrict the transmission of identifiable clinical text across institutional boundaries. This setting raises two challenges: existing medical agent systems often rely on textual evidence exchange, while raw latent states such as hidden states and KV caches may still reveal prompt-derived clinical content. We introduce MedLatentDx, a latent multi-agent communication framework in which hospital agents keep private clinical records and retrieved cases local, and send compact latent KV blocks to a host agent for rare-disease diagnosis. MedLatentDx supports two deployment settings: same-backbone hospital agents use latent KV distillation, while hospitals with different LLM backbones use cross-family latent alignment. On CrossRare-Bench, a self-built large-scale rare-disease benchmark with hospital-level partitions, MedLatentDx improves cross-hospital diagnostic performance while reducing reconstructable clinical content relative to raw-latent communication baselines.
tldr: MedLatentDx proposes a latent multi-agent communication framework that uses compact latent KV blocks for privacy-preserving cross-hospital rare-disease diagnosis, outperforming raw-latent baselines on a new benchmark.
tldr_zh: MedLatentDx 提出了一种潜在多智能体通信框架，通过紧凑的潜在 KV 块实现跨医院罕见病诊断的隐私保护，在新基准上优于原始潜在基线。
summary_zh: 摘要：罕见疾病涵盖超过7,000种病症，影响逾3亿患者，然而任何单一医院都难以积累足够多的某一病例以实现可靠诊断。跨医院协作可通过允许诊断机构利用分布式、病例特定的诊断证据来提供帮助，但隐私法规限制了可识别临床文本在机构间的传输。这一场景带来两大挑战：现有医疗智能体系统常依赖文本证据交换，而原始潜在状态（如隐藏状态和KV缓存）仍可能泄露基于提示的临床内容。我们提出MedLatentDx——一种潜在多智能体通信框架，其中医院智能体将私有临床记录和检索到的病例保留在本地，并向宿主智能体发送紧凑的潜在KV块以进行罕见病诊断。MedLatentDx支持两种部署模式：采用相同骨干模型的医院智能体使用潜在KV蒸馏，而使用不同LLM骨干的医院则采用跨家族潜在对齐。在自建的大规模罕见病基准CrossRare-Bench（含医院级数据划分）上，MedLatentDx在提升跨医院诊断性能的同时，相较于原始潜在通信基线减少了可重建的临床内容。

title: Robustness without Wrinkles: Parallel Simulation and Robust MPC for Certified Deformable Manipulation
summary: We present CORD-SLS, a real-time control method for safe deformable object manipulation, with a focus on ropes and cloth. At its core is a GPU-parallel differentiable simulator with contact smoothing which enables efficient gradient-based planning through intermittent contact. To robustly satisfy constraints under model and sensing uncertainty, we develop a real-time, GPU-parallel output-feedback robust model predictive control (MPC) algorithm that plans with this simulator. We further show that the simulator accelerates model-based RL for training neural manipulation policies. To improve real-world robustness, we use conformal prediction to calibrate visual-feedback and perception-error bounds for MPC, producing reachable tubes that enable high-probability safe control. We evaluate CORD-SLS on high-dimensional, contact-rich rope and cloth manipulation tasks in simulation and hardware, including obstacle avoidance, routing, folding, and smoothing. Across settings, CORD-SLS achieves millisecond-speed planning, exceeding baselines in safety, speed, and task success.
tldr: A real-time control method for safe deformable manipulation (ropes and cloth) using GPU-parallel differentiable simulation, robust MPC with output feedback, and conformal prediction for certified safety.
tldr_zh: 一种用于安全变形物体（绳索和布料）操作的实时控制方法，采用GPU并行可微仿真、带输出反馈的鲁棒模型预测控制以及保形预测来确保安全。
summary_zh: 我们提出CORD-SLS，一种面向绳索与布料等可变形物体安全操控的实时控制方法。其核心是一个基于GPU并行计算并具有接触平滑处理的可微分仿真器，能够通过间歇性接触实现高效的基于梯度的规划。为在模型与感知不确定性下鲁棒地满足约束条件，我们开发了一种实时、GPU并行的输出反馈鲁棒模型预测控制（MPC）算法，该算法利用该仿真器进行规划。我们进一步证明该仿真器能够加速基于模型的强化学习，用于训练神经操控策略。为提升实际环境中的鲁棒性，我们采用保形预测来校准MPC的视觉反馈与感知误差边界，生成可达管集，从而实现高概率的安全控制。我们在仿真与硬件上对CORD-SLS进行了评估，涉及绳索与布料的高维、密集接触操控任务，包括避障、布线、折叠与展平。在各种设置下，CORD-SLS均实现了毫秒级规划速度，在安全性、速度与任务成功率上均超越基线方法。

title: Can Post-Training Turn LLMs into Good Medical Coders? An Empirical Study of Generative ICD Coding
summary: Automated International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding is a core medical-coding task for billing, epidemiology, and clinical decision support. Generative large language models (LLMs) are often reported as weak medical coders, but this finding mainly comes from inference-time settings such as prompting, retrieval, reranking, or tool use, leaving the role of task-specific post-training underexplored. We present a controlled empirical study of post-training for generative ICD coding, comparing discriminative baselines with LLM coders across prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning under a common protocol and metric set. To our knowledge, this is the first study to evaluate RL-based post-training for generative LLM coders in ICD coding. We further introduce PHI, a diagnostic curriculum that extends GRPO to refine missed-code cases. Our results show that prompting-only evaluation substantially underestimates the potential of LLMs for ICD coding. SFT provides the main capability jump, GRPO further improves code-set prediction beyond SFT, and PHI provides targeted gains on macro-level performance. These findings suggest that the main bottleneck is not the generative formulation alone, but how the model is adapted and optimized for full-taxonomy recall. We release our code, data splits, and checkpoints at https://github.com/AlexandreWANG915/LLM4ICD.
tldr: This paper empirically studies post-training techniques (SFT, GRPO, and a novel PHI curriculum) for generative LLMs on ICD coding, showing that prompting underestimates their potential and that post-training significantly improves performance, especially with RL-based methods.
tldr_zh: 本文通过实证研究了生成式大语言模型在ICD编码任务上的后训练技术（SFT、GRPO以及新提出的PHI课程），发现仅用提示词评估低估了潜力，后训练（尤其是基于强化学习的方法）能显著提升性能。
summary_zh: 自动国际疾病分类（ICD）编码是用于计费、流行病学和临床决策支持的核心医学编码任务。生成式大语言模型（LLM）常被报道为弱医学编码器，但这一发现主要来自提示、检索、重排序或工具使用等推理时设置，而任务特定的后训练作用尚未得到充分探索。我们提出了一项关于生成式ICD编码后训练的受控实证研究，在共同的协议和度量集下，通过提示、监督微调和强化学习，将判别式基线与LLM编码器进行了比较。据我们所知，这是首个评估基于强化学习的后训练用于生成式LLM编码器在ICD编码中的研究。我们进一步引入了PHI，一种扩展GRPO以优化漏码病例的诊断课程。我们的结果表明，仅通过提示评估会严重低估LLM在ICD编码中的潜力。监督微调提供了主要的能力跃升，GRPO在监督微调基础上进一步改善了编码集预测，而PHI则在宏观性能上提供了针对性的提升。这些发现表明，主要瓶颈并非仅在于生成式公式本身，而在于模型如何针对完整分类体系召回进行适配和优化。我们在https://github.com/AlexandreWANG915/LLM4ICD发布了我们的代码、数据划分和检查点。

title: More with LESS -- Local Scene Representations for Tactile Imaging
summary: Tactile imaging seeks to reconstruct the internal structure of soft objects through touch sensing, with applications in medical diagnosis and robotic manipulation. Recent self-supervised learning approaches have shown promising results, but rely on global, unstructured representations and robot-controlled sensing, limiting generalization and practical use. We propose Local Encoder for Spatial Sensing (LESS), an object-centric tactile representation that exploits the local nature of touch. The tactile scene is modeled as a grid of recurrent encoders with local receptive fields, whose states are fused to reconstruct 2D or 3D images of internal structure. This compositional design enables strong generalization: models trained on single-inclusion phantoms accurately image objects with multiple inclusions and varying sizes. The local structure further supports spatial uncertainty estimation. In addition, we enable hand-held tactile imaging via external pose tracking and human-like palpation data, and extend tactile imaging to full 3D reconstruction.
tldr: This paper proposes LESS, a local encoder for spatial sensing that uses grid-based recurrent encoders to reconstruct 2D/3D internal structures of soft objects from tactile data, enabling strong generalization and hand-held operation with pose tracking.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出LESS，一种基于网格递归编码器的局部空间传感方法，通过触觉数据重建软物体的内部2D/3D结构，支持强泛化能力和手持式操作（结合位姿跟踪）。
summary_zh: 触觉成像旨在通过触觉感知重建软物体的内部结构，在医学诊断和机器人操作中具有应用前景。近年来自监督学习方法已展现出潜力，但其依赖全局非结构化表示及机器人控制的传感方式，限制了泛化能力与实际应用。我们提出空间感知局部编码器（LESS），这是一种以物体为中心的触觉表示方法，利用了触觉的局部特性。触觉场景被建模为由具有局部感受野的循环编码器构成的网格，这些编码器的状态被融合以重建内部结构的二维或三维图像。这种组合设计实现了强大的泛化能力：在单内含物仿体上训练的模型能够准确成像具有多个内含物及不同尺寸的物体。局部结构还支持空间不确定性估计。此外，我们通过外部位姿跟踪和类人触诊数据实现了手持式触觉成像，并将触觉成像扩展到完整的三维重建。

title: Learning Dynamic Swing-Up of an Inverted Pendulum using Remote Magnetic Actuation
summary: Electromagnetic Navigation Systems (eMNS) have gained considerable attention for minimally invasive surgery and targeted drug delivery. While most of the literature relies on quasi-static control of these systems, recent work has demonstrated the benefits of dynamic approaches. However, trajectory tracking far from equilibrium states remains largely unaddressed. We close this gap by demonstrating the first swing-up of a magnetically actuated inverted pendulum using the clinically-ready Navion eMNS. Although the inverted pendulum is not clinically relevant in itself, the proposed method utilizes torques and forces as control objectives, making it applicable to other magnetically actuated devices such as catheters and guidewires. Our approach combines trajectory optimization that accounts for internal eMNS dynamics with time-varying Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) state feedback and Iterative Learning Control (ILC), which leverages previous trial data and the system's dynamic model to progressively refine the feedforward command. While LQR alone fails due to the complex phenomena of magnetic actuation, ILC enables successful swing-up within six iterations. Furthermore, post-experimental analysis reveals that the learned ILC correction closely matches the torque discrepancy predicted by high-fidelity magnetic field model calibration, suggesting learning and adaptation as a promising tool to deal with uncertainties in electromagnetic actuation arising, e.g., from patient-specific physiological motion patterns and field model calibration inaccuracies.
tldr: This paper presents the first successful dynamic swing-up of a magnetically actuated inverted pendulum using a clinically-ready electromagnetic navigation system, combining trajectory optimization, time-varying LQR, and iterative learning control to handle uncertainties.
tldr_zh: 本文首次利用临床级电磁导航系统成功实现了磁驱动倒立摆的动态摆起，结合轨迹优化、时变LQR和迭代学习控制来处理不确定性。
summary_zh: 电磁导航系统（eMNS）在微创手术和靶向药物递送领域引起了广泛关注。尽管现有文献大多依赖于这些系统的准静态控制，但近期研究已证明了动态方法的优势。然而，远离平衡态的轨迹跟踪仍未得到充分解决。我们通过利用临床级Navion电磁导航系统，首次实现了磁驱动倒立摆的摆起，从而弥补了这一空白。虽然倒立摆本身不具备临床相关性，但所提出的方法以力矩和力作为控制目标，使其可适用于其他磁驱动装置，如导管和导丝。我们的方法结合了考虑内部电磁导航系统动力学的轨迹优化、时变线性二次型调节器（LQR）状态反馈以及迭代学习控制（ILC），后者利用先前试验数据和系统动力学模型逐步优化前馈指令。单独使用LQR因磁驱动的复杂现象而失败，而ILC在六次迭代内成功实现了摆起。此外，实验后分析表明，学习得到的ILC修正量与高保真磁场模型校准所预测的力矩偏差高度吻合，这表明学习和自适应是处理电磁驱动中不确定性的有效工具，这些不确定性可能源于患者特异性生理运动模式及磁场模型校准误差等。

title: Expert-Driven Survival Machines: Improving Stratification and Interpretability in Multiple Clinical Cohorts
summary: Survival prediction plays a central role for healthcare providers and clinical researchers. Accurate risk stratification enables early intervention and improved patient management. Most existing deep survival models learn one common feature representation for all patients, which may hide important differences between patient subgroups. In contrast, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework allows different parts of the model to focus on different patient patterns, leading to more individualized representations. Therefore, in this work, we propose a mixture-of-experts enhanced adaptive deep clustering survival framework (AdaCSM) for modeling such heterogeneous survival patterns. We introduce a routing-based expert mechanism that enables conditional specialization within a parametric survival modeling framework. The proposed architecture allocates patients to specialized risk predictors dynamically while preserving the patient survival and subtype clustering objectives. We compare our method with state-of-the-art survival and deep clustering models on multiple real-world longitudinal clinical cohorts spanning diverse disease domains. The proposed method demonstrates improved predictive performance and leads to interpretable results in survival analysis.
tldr: This paper proposes a Mixture-of-Experts enhanced adaptive deep clustering survival framework (AdaCSM) that dynamically allocates patients to specialized risk predictors, improving stratification and interpretability in survival analysis across multiple clinical cohorts.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种混合专家增强的自适应深度聚类生存框架（AdaCSM），该框架动态地将患者分配给专门的风险预测器，在多个临床队列的生存分析中提高了分层和可解释性。
summary_zh: 生存预测在医疗提供者和临床研究中扮演核心角色。准确的风险分层能够实现早期干预并改善患者管理。现有大多数深度生存模型为所有患者学习单一共同特征表示，这可能掩盖不同患者亚组之间的重要差异。相比之下，专家混合（MoE）框架允许模型的不同部分关注不同的患者模式，从而产生更具个性化的表示。因此，本文提出一种基于专家混合增强的自适应深度聚类生存框架（AdaCSM），用于建模此类异质性生存模式。我们引入了一种基于路由的专家机制，可在参数化生存建模框架中实现条件性专化。所提出的架构动态地将患者分配给专门的风险预测器，同时保留患者生存与亚型聚类目标。我们在涵盖多种疾病领域的多个真实世界纵向临床队列上，将我们的方法与最先进的生存模型和深度聚类模型进行了比较。所提出的方法展示了改进的预测性能，并在生存分析中产生了可解释的结果。
